title: Adversarial Bandit Convex Optimization with $d^{3/2}\sqrt{n}$ Regret
abstract: arXiv:2611.33531v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: We study adversarial bandit convex optimization, where in each of $n$ rounds a learner chooses a point $A_t$ in a convex body $\mathcal{K}\subset\mathbb{R}^d$ and observes only a noisy value of a convex loss $f_t:\mathcal{K}\to[0,1]$ at that point. The losses are chosen by an adversary, who may change them from round to round and adapt them to the learner's past actions. We improve the best known regret bound for this problem from $\widetilde O(d^{5/2}\sqrt n)$ (Lattimore, 2020, 2026) to $\widetilde O(d^{3/2}\sqrt n)$, which matches the rate conjectured by Bubeck et al. (2017). Together with the recent lower bound of $\Omega(d^{4/3}\sqrt n)$ due to Rajaraman and Han (2026), it determines the minimax regret up to a factor of $d^{1/6}$ and logarithmic factors. The algorithm is an online Newton step with Gaussian exploration. Unlike earlier methods of this kind, it uses unbiased estimates of the gradient and Hessian of the Gaussian smooth

translated_title: 具有 $d^{3/2}\sqrt{n}$ 遗憾的对抗性赌博机凸优化
translated_abstract: 我们研究对抗性赌博机凸优化问题：在 $n$ 轮中的每一轮，学习者选择凸体 $\mathcal{K}\subset\mathbb{R}^d$ 中的一个点 $A_t$，并仅观测到该点处凸损失函数 $f_t:\mathcal{K}\to[0,1]$ 的含噪值。损失函数由对手选择，对手可以逐轮改变损失函数，并根据学习者过去的动作进行自适应调整。我们将该问题目前已知的最佳遗憾界从 $\widetilde O(d^{5/2}\sqrt n)$（Lattimore, 2020, 2026）改进为 $\widetilde O(d^{3/2}\sqrt n)$，这与 Bubeck 等人（2017）所猜测的速率相匹配。结合 Rajaraman 和 Han（2026）最近给出的 $\Omega(d^{4/3}\sqrt n)$ 下界，该结果将极小极大遗憾确定到 $d^{1/6}$ 因子和对数因子范围之内。该算法是带高斯探索的在线牛顿步方法。与以往同类方法不同，它使用高斯平滑后函数的梯度与 Hessian 矩阵的无偏估计……
tldr: 本文提出一种带高斯探索的在线牛顿步算法，将对抗性赌博机凸优化的遗憾上界从 $\widetilde O(d^{5/2}\sqrt n)$ 改进为 $\widetilde O(d^{3/2}\sqrt n)$，匹配了此前被猜想的最优速率，并将极小极大遗憾确定到 $d^{1/6}$ 因子以内。
en_tdlr: This paper improves the best known regret bound for adversarial bandit convex optimization from $\widetilde O(d^{5/2}\sqrt n)$ to $\widetilde O(d^{3/2}\sqrt n)$ via an online Newton step with Gaussian exploration, matching the conjectured optimal rate and pinning down the minimax regret up to a factor of $d^{1/6}$.
